title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page does not belong to the De Rham / divided-power notes. It is page 115 of the typescript of SGA 7 I, Exposé IX (Grothendieck, 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie'), §9.5, filed into cote 136. It may have been reused as scrap paper or simply misfiled; the neighbouring pages are manuscript notes on C^{DR,pd}.

The mathematics:
- Setting: S is a henselian trait with generic point η and ℓ a prime. The data are ℓ-divisible (Barsotti–Tate) pro-ℓ-groups P, Q, R over S. P is of multiplicative type and Q is étale; R is the middle graded piece. E and F are two-step extensions over S sharing R, roughly E = extension involving R and P, and F = extension involving Q and R.
- Extension panachée (in the sense of SGA 7 IX §9.3): X_η is a BT pro-ℓ-group over η with a three-step filtration. Its partial extensions are identified with E_η and F_η.
- Level n: passing to each truncation X(n), one gets a panachée extension of E(n)_η by F(n)_η.
- The pairing (9.4.1): §9.4 attaches to such an extension a bilinear pairing c(X(n)_η) : Q(n) ⊗ Q*(n) → Λ_n = Z/ℓ^{n+1}. Here Q*(n) = D(P(n)) is the Cartier dual of the multiplicative part, a finite étale group. The pairing is essentially the Kummer-theoretic invariant of the induced extension of the étale part by the multiplicative part over η, using henselianity.
- Passage to the limit: the pairings are compatible in n. They give a morphism of twisted constant ℓ-adic sheaves c(X_η) : Q ⊗ Q* → Z_{ℓ,S}.
- Proposition 9.5.6 (stated in passing, henselian hypothesis dropped) concerns the generic-fibre functor X ↦ X_η from panachée BT extensions of E by F over S. The page breaks off before the conclusion. In SGA 7 it characterizes which generic extensions extend over S, in terms of the vanishing or integrality of this pairing.

Purpose: this is the ℓ-adic / Barsotti–Tate analogue of the monodromy pairing for semi-stable abelian varieties. It feeds the orthogonality theorem and the Néron component-group pairing of Exposé IX.
